newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to sack former aide from army.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to sack former aide from army.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has decided to sack former aide Alexander Korzhakov from the Russian army because of "lies" he told about the Russian leader and his family, the Kremlin said on Monday.

Korzhakov, once a close friend of Yeltsin who was dismissed as chief Kremlin bodyguard in June, has publicly accused presidential chief of staff Anatoly Chubais of seeking to seize real power and said Yeltsin's daughter was in league with him.
He has hinted he is ready to disclose confidential information which could prove explosive on the Russian political scene.

"After his sacking on June 20, 1996, Lieutenant-General Alexander Korzhakov has come out with a series of lies concerning the Russian president and members of his family," said an order released by Yeltsin's press office on Monday.

"He (Korzhakov) has allowed himself to publish confidential information he obtained in office. Korzhakov's public threats to disclose information that he possesses are aimed at discrediting top state officials," said the order signed on Sunday.
The statement said Yeltsin had ordered his security service to prepare the paperwork for sacking Korzhakov from the Russian army.

Korzhakov remained a member of the Russian armed forces with the rank of lieutenant-general after Yeltsin sacked him as chief of the Kremlin security force to improve his own chances of winning a second term in office.
It was not clear if Korzhakov would also be stripped of his military rank under the new order.

Korzhakov, who stood by Yeltsin for 11 years of his stormy career, accused Chubais of trying to establish his own "regency" in Russia and said Yeltsin's daughter Tatyana Dyachenko had teamed up with Chubais.
